title: Credit and Collections Policy: Bill Credit Window for a Payment Arrangements Early Payoff
content:
**Credit and Collections Policy — Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements): how far back bill credits are considered at an early payoff**

**Section 1.** How far back credits are considered at an early payoff follows the household's circumstances on the member's Electric Service by Rate Schedule account on the payoff day:

(a) where the service account carries an unexpired medical certificate on the payoff day and an outstanding disconnect notice, the bill credits posted in the 12 months ending on the payoff day are considered;

(b) where it carries an unexpired medical certificate and no outstanding disconnect notice, those posted in the 11 months ending on the payoff day;

(c) where it carries no unexpired medical certificate, those posted in the month ending on the payoff day.

**Section 2.** The bill credits are those posted to the service account, by posting date, within the window of Section 1; the capital credit retirement credits and the deposit interest credits among them are each totalled over that same window.

**Section 3 — terms.** A medical certificate is unexpired on the payoff day when the medical certificate expiry date on the service account is the payoff day or later. A disconnect notice is outstanding when the service account shows a disconnect notice date.

| Unexpired medical certificate on the payoff day | Outstanding disconnect notice | Window of bill credits considered |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 12 months ending on the payoff day |
| yes | no | 11 months ending on the payoff day |
| no | yes | 1 month ending on the payoff day |
| no | no | 1 month ending on the payoff day |

**Hypothetical:** a capital credit retirement bill credit posted five months before the payoff day falls within the window under (a) and (b), and outside it under (c).
